draft.title: Genotype and phenotype
card: the alleles an organism carries for a gene. An allele is one version of a gene. For example, a pea plant may carry the alleles for tall and short stems.
the trait that can be observed, such as stem height, flower colour or blood type.
The genotype sets what an organism can become. The environment also affects the phenotype. A plant with alleles for tall growth may stay short if it has too little water or light.
Organisms with the same genotype can have different phenotypes if their environments differ. Organisms with different genotypes can sometimes have the same phenotype.
draft.remember: Genotype is the alleles carried. Phenotype is the trait seen, shaped by genotype and environment.

a.q: Which of these describes a genotype?
opts: The pair of alleles a rabbit carries for fur colour
The brown fur colour that can be seen on a rabbit
The height a rabbit reaches after a good diet
The number of rabbits in a population
a.why: A genotype is the alleles an organism carries, so the pair of alleles for fur colour is a genotype. Brown fur is tempting but it is the trait that shows, which is the phenotype.
a.clue: Genotype is about what is inside the cells, not what can be seen.

b.q: Two genetically identical seedlings are grown. One gets full sunlight and grows tall. The other is kept in dim light and stays short. What does this show?
opts: Same genotype, but the environment changed the phenotype
Different genotypes caused the different heights
Same phenotype, because the alleles are identical
The dim light changed the alleles in the short plant
b.why: The seedlings are genetically identical, so they share a genotype. Their heights differ because light affected the phenotype. The environment did not change the alleles, so the idea that the dim light altered them is wrong.
b.clue: The seedlings are identical in their alleles. What differs is their surroundings.

a.best: The pair of alleles a rabbit carries for fur colour

b.best: Same genotype, but the environment changed the phenotype

problems.detail: Seedlings grown in dim light usually etiolate, growing taller and spindlier than those in full sun, not shorter. A student who knows this may be confused. Water shortage or poor nutrients would be a safer example of the environment keeping a plant short.

'May stay short if it has too little water or light': low light often makes stems elongate (etiolation), so light is a misleading example of the environment stunting height. Water or nutrients would be better.

The clue says genotype is 'inside the cells, not what can be seen', which implies phenotype is only what is visible. The card lists blood type, which is not visible, as a phenotype, so the clue misstates the distinction.
